faq.heading: This is probably what's on your mind

items.q: How long does the process take?
items.a:
Every project is unique and has its own complexity.
That said, we typically reach a working prototype within just a few weeks.
A full product build including strategic spec, design, and content writing takes 3–4 months.

For any timeline estimate, we'll align on clear expectations right at the start of the project.

items.q: What's the final deliverable I'll receive?
items.a: At the end of the spec process, our clients receive an interactive prototype you can click and feel, a strategic spec document, design files, and clear guidelines that let you move forward independently (or continue the project with us).

items.q: I've already done a spec process — what's unique about your work?
items.a:
Our methodology is unique and doesn't exist at other studios (as far as we know).
Our entire process is built on certainty for our clients. It's important to us that you see the product's user experience before committing to development (which is the expensive and lengthy part).

Instead of a PDF that gets shelved or a Figma link, you get a working prototype you can click and understand the user experience.
For the first time, in just a few weeks you can experience the product and refine it quickly.

items.q: What's the difference between a prototype and a finished product?
items.a:
A prototype is an interactive model that simulates the user experience.
It's not final code and doesn't include the precise visual design.
But it lets you feel, test, and refine your product before investing in development.

items.q: How much does it cost to work together?
items.a:
Every project is priced according to its size and complexity.
We'd love to talk and understand what you're building, then tailor a precise proposal.

items.q: What happens after we get the prototype?
items.a: You move on to development with all the files and reports. You're not dependent on us — but we're here if you need guidance in the design and development stage too.
